characters.name: Kaito
characters.want: To protect his cherished memories without losing his family.
characters.personality: Curious, emotional, brave, and reflective with spiky brown hair, dark blue hoodie, and blue eyes.

characters.name: Mia
characters.want: To stay close to her big brother and play together.
characters.personality: Innocent, sweet, affectionate with long braided auburn hair and yellow sweater.

characters.name: Marcus
characters.want: To enforce the rule of memory exchange at midnight.
characters.personality: Tall, mysterious, emotionless hooded figure with pale glowing eyes.

characters.name: Mom
characters.want: To nurture and protect her children.
characters.personality: Warm, loving, gentle with wavy black hair and beige cardigan.

lines.text: At midnight, a shadowy corridor opens to a terrifying realm of choices.
lines.say: (nervous) At midnight, a shadowy corridor opens to a terrifying realm of choices.
lines.speaker: narrator
lines.scene: A dark long hallway appears with three towering mysterious wooden doors illuminated by eerie glowing lights.

lines.text: Every midnight, three doors appear in my hallway. You can enter only one.
lines.say: (nervous) Every midnight, three doors appear in my hallway. You can enter only one.
lines.speaker: narrator
lines.scene: Kaito stands terrified in the dark hallway as three massive doors loom ahead.

lines.text: But whichever door you choose… you lose a memory forever.
lines.say: (nervous) But whichever door you choose… you lose a memory forever.
lines.speaker: narrator
lines.scene: Kaito reaches his trembling hand toward the glowing red door while a tall shadow rises behind him.

lines.text: Choose carefully, boy. One door will show you happiness. One will show you pain.
lines.say: (serious) Choose carefully, boy. One door will show you happiness. One will show you pain.
lines.speaker: narrator
lines.scene: Marcus the Doorkeeper emerges from the darkness holding an old silver pocket watch.

lines.text: And one will show you what you have yet to lose.
lines.say: (serious) And one will show you what you have yet to lose.
lines.speaker: narrator
lines.scene: Marcus points his thin pale hand toward the white and blue glowing doors.

lines.text: What happens if I don’t choose?
lines.say: (worried) What happens if I don’t choose?
lines.speaker: narrator
lines.scene: Kaito steps back cautiously, questioning the tall mysterious figure.

lines.text: Then the doors will choose for you.
lines.say: (serious) Then the doors will choose for you.
lines.speaker: narrator
lines.scene: Marcus slowly turns his featureless face back toward Kaito.

lines.text: Come on, you two. Dinner is ready!
lines.say: (happy) Come on, you two. Dinner is ready!
lines.speaker: narrator
lines.scene: The red door opens slightly spilling warm light into the hallway where young Kaito and Mia play with Mom.

lines.text: Behind the red door was my happiest memory. A time when my family was still together.
lines.say: (sad) Behind the red door was my happiest memory. A time when my family was still together.
lines.speaker: narrator
lines.scene: Kaito watches the joyful flashback of his family laughing together in the cozy room.

lines.text: Enter… and you will never feel that happiness again.
lines.say: (serious) Enter… and you will never feel that happiness again.
lines.speaker: narrator
lines.scene: Marcus whispers chillingly into Kaito's ear as the warm red light fades.

lines.text: Behind the blue door was the worst night of my life. The night I lost my mother.
lines.say: (sad) Behind the blue door was the worst night of my life. The night I lost my mother.
lines.speaker: narrator
lines.scene: The blue door swings open revealing a rainy hospital hallway where young Kaito sits weeping beside Mia.

lines.text: I don’t want to remember that night anymore.
lines.say: (sad) I don’t want to remember that night anymore.
lines.speaker: narrator
lines.scene: Kaito looks down with trembling lips as painful memories flood his mind.

lines.text: Pain is still a memory, boy. And memories are what make you who you are.
lines.say: (serious) Pain is still a memory, boy. And memories are what make you who you are.
lines.speaker: narrator
lines.scene: Marcus gazes impassively at Kaito as icy wind blows from the blue door.

lines.text: You’re late, big brother!
lines.say: (happy) You’re late, big brother!
lines.speaker: narrator
lines.scene: The white door glows golden and opens to reveal an older Kaito sitting with Mia.

lines.text: Behind the white door was a memory I had never lived. A future where Emma was still beside me.
lines.say: (worried) Behind the white door was a memory I had never lived. A future where Emma was still beside me.
lines.speaker: narrator
lines.scene: Kaito stares shocked at the unwritten future scene inside the white door.

lines.text: Is that… my future?
lines.say: (worried) Is that… my future?
lines.speaker: narrator
lines.scene: Kaito whispers softly to himself, overwhelmed by what he sees.

lines.text: Some memories haven’t happened yet. But you can still lose them.
lines.say: (serious) Some memories haven’t happened yet. But you can still lose them.
lines.speaker: narrator
lines.scene: Marcus steps closer to Kaito, explaining the stakes of the final choice.

lines.text: Why do you keep taking people’s memories?
lines.say: (angry) Why do you keep taking people’s memories?
lines.speaker: narrator
lines.scene: Kaito turns angrily to Marcus as the silver watch reflects photos of his loved ones.

lines.text: Because people would rather forget their pain than remember the people they loved.
lines.say: (serious) Because people would rather forget their pain than remember the people they loved.
lines.speaker: narrator
lines.scene: Marcus tilts his head down and speaks with solemn truth.

lines.text: Then I choose none of them.
lines.say: (confident) Then I choose none of them.
lines.speaker: narrator
lines.scene: Kaito takes a firm step away from all three doors with fierce determination.

lines.text: You’re the first person who ever refused.
lines.say: (worried) You’re the first person who ever refused.
lines.speaker: narrator
lines.scene: Marcus stands completely still in surprise as the three doors dissolve into mist.

lines.text: I finally understood. You don’t have to erase painful memories to move forward.
lines.say: (happy) I finally understood. You don’t have to erase painful memories to move forward.
lines.speaker: narrator
lines.scene: Kaito wakes up in his sunlit bedroom holding an old framed photo of his mother and sister.

lines.text: Sometimes, remembering is how you keep the people you love alive.
lines.say: (happy) Sometimes, remembering is how you keep the people you love alive.
lines.speaker: narrator
lines.scene: Kaito smiles warmly while clutching the family photo close to his heart.

lines.text: If you were trapped in this hallway, which door would you choose to enter?
lines.say: (soft tone) If you were trapped in this hallway, which door would you choose to enter?
lines.speaker: narrator
lines.scene: A choice prompt appears asking the audience which door they would enter.

lines.text: Comment below your final answer: RED, BLUE, WHITE, or NONE!
lines.say: (confident) Comment below your final answer: RED, BLUE, WHITE, or NONE!
lines.speaker: narrator

owner_text:
At midnight, a shadowy corridor opens to a terrifying realm of choices.
Every midnight, three doors appear in my hallway. You can enter only one.
But whichever door you choose… you lose a memory forever.
Choose carefully, boy. One door will show you happiness. One will show you pain.
And one will show you what you have yet to lose.
What happens if I don’t choose?
Then the doors will choose for you.
Come on, you two. Dinner is ready!
Behind the red door was my happiest memory. A time when my family was still together.
Enter… and you will never feel that happiness again.
Behind the blue door was the worst night of my life. The night I lost my mother.
I don’t want to remember that night anymore.
Pain is still a memory, boy. And memories are what make you who you are.
You’re late, big brother!
Behind the white door was a memory I had never lived. A future where Emma was still beside me.
Is that… my future?
Some memories haven’t happened yet. But you can still lose them.
Why do you keep taking people’s memories?
Because people would rather forget their pain than remember the people they loved.
Then I choose none of them.
You’re the first person who ever refused.
I finally understood. You don’t have to erase painful memories to move forward.
Sometimes, remembering is how you keep the people you love alive.
If you were trapped in this hallway, which door would you choose to enter?
